column7: Target-aware lower modes preserve host ABI while selecting scalar or SIMD lowering.
System V and Win64 C aggregate layout classes intentionally differ.
Win64 aggregate diagnostics describe the target-specific supported slice.
Win64 scalar-field aggregate eligibility differs from System V integer-only fields.
Win64 register aggregate sizes are limited to 1, 2, 4, or 8 bytes.
C ABI diagnostics report the concrete target triple.
System V two-register aggregate return diagnostic is target-specific.
Internal aggregate classification selects Win64 versus System V transport from the lowering mode.
Internal aggregate classification accepts Win64 aggregate transport only in Win64 ABI modes.
The C ABI axis of a lower mode: Linux-target modes select System V, Windows-target modes Win64.
Combined C ABI helper intentionally delegates to target-specific ABI predicates.
Linux-target lower modes select System V C ABI lowering.
Rebuilding a mode from its axes keeps the target ABI while changing the ISA mode (source dispatch).
Target-aware lower modes project onto the same SIMD axis as the target-neutral modes.
Windows-target lower modes select Win64 C ABI lowering.
The return-storage authority records the lowering mode's C ABI (Win64 or System V).
A C extern's hidden return storage follows the Win64 or System V convention of the lowering mode.
